data.content_ref: inline:SRC_004 depends on SRC_002: the directed-suppression mechanism (over-suppression of low-energy saddle-crossing) inherits the lineage-dependency tax, because without the tax there is no cost asymmetry between within-basin descent and cross-basin exploration, and thus no directed bias. This dependence is REFUTED IF the saddle-crossing costs are intrinsic to the problem space and independent of the allocation regime—i.e., if rival lineages face identical saddle heights regardless of ownership.
